author: ADAM AUCOIN Staff Writer
title: Woodstock field hockey holds off Otter Valley, 3-2 | Local | timesargus.com
text:
BRANDON — Division III field hockey has been Montpelier's kingdom for the last handful of years. The Solons have have won three of the last four D-III titles and the one time they didn't win it all, they were the state runner-up.
There are a handful of teams hoping to knock Montpelier off that pedestal this fall. One of those squads is Woodstock, who took the Solons to double overtime in championship game last year.
The Wasps are off to a good start in their quest and have made it through the first half of the season without a loss. Woodstock earned a tight 3-2 victory over Division II Otter Valley Wednesday afternoon.
It was an early surge by Woodstock that proved to be the difference in the game. The Wasps scored twice in the opening quarter and had the Otters playing catch-up the rest of the way.
"The last few games, we've been challenged to get going," said Woodstock coach Leanne Tapley. "The first quarter has been a harder quarter for us. This field was fast and we have a lot of fast girls, so it definitely played to us.
"I played 20 something girls. They were working together and they were helping each other. The score looked close, but I think we definitely dominated"
Two of Woodstock's speedy girls teamed up for the game's first goal when super-skilled junior Betta Cirovic drove at the defense and shipped off to a classmate Lindsey St. Cyr, who was in the perfect spot on the right post to put the Wasps ahead within the first minute of the game.
Another speedster for Woodstock senior captain Grace Perreault dribbled through the circle and put one inside the left post with 3:34 left in the opening quarter to give the Wasps the early two-goal edge.
"Grace has been waiting all season to play on a fast field. Our field in Woodstock is so thick and she trips on it," Tapley said. "It's so nice for her to get the ball on a field like this. It just moves."
Woodstock had a big edge in possession, but the Otters did well to keep the deficit in check. A big part of OV's effort in doing that was sophomore goalie Sofia Kerr, who was excellent all game long.
Kerr had a handful of incredible sprawling saves that kept the Otters afloat and was excellent in her decision-making coming off the line to kick a ball away. The small but talented goalie had 11 saves in the contest.
It took the Otters a little bit of time to pick it up on offense and OV coach Jodie Keith pointed to communication as a point of emphasis for her squad.
"They needed to pick up the pace and find a little energy. I think as the game progressed it got a little bit better," Keith said. "The biggest thing for us is communication. They're not quiet in practice but when they can close up a little bit."
Otter Valley pulled within one on multiple occasions in the second half. The Otters scored with 5:30 left the third quarter with senior captain Sophie Parker putting one home in a congested circle on a penalty corner.
Woodstock responded two minutes later with Perreault's second goal of the contest.
Otter Valley kept pushing in the fourth and found another breakthrough with 3:19 to play as Tayah Cram fed senior classmate Parker for a goal.
"Playing from behind is never easy. In years past, we'd play from behind and we just shut down and don't score any more goals," Keith said. "I'm glad to see that this young group has some fight in them."
Freshman goalie Sadie Rowlee had three saves for Woodstock.
Otter Valley (2-3-1) will look to snap a three-game losing skid on Wednesday, hosting rival Fair Haven.
Woodstock (6-0-1) has continued to establish itself as one of the favorites to to win it all in Division III.
If they do reach the state final, it would be played at Burr and Burton Academy. Funny enough, that is exactly the place the Wasps will be on Friday afternoon, taking on the Bulldogs.
